solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Grandeur that is recalled by one ancient city (7)

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters come back to front

annotation.surface: A remark on the lost splendour of a city of antiquity.
annotation.walkthrough: The grandeur in the surface is the ruins' faded glory; in the wordplay it is simply POMP, the first chunk of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman city buried by Vesuvius in AD 79.

clue.text: Give a word of thanks for tomato sauce (7)

annotation.surface: Someone saying thank you for being handed the tomato sauce at table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ta' is everyday British for 'thanks'. The surface makes 'Give a word of thanks' one instruction; it splits into three chunks.
annotation.definitionFit: Passata is sieved uncooked tomato, used as a sauce base in Italian cooking.

clue.text: Child transfixed by cross monster (8)

indicators.note: to be transfixed is to be run through, so the child has the cross stuck inside it

blocks.note: a minor = a child in law
a tau cross is T-shaped; tau is the Greek letter T

annotation.surface: A child frozen in fear by an angry monster.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry and 'transfixed' as frozen with fear; in fact the cross is a shape and it spears the child: MINO(TAU)R.
annotation.definitionFit: The Minotaur was the bull-headed monster of Greek myth kept in the Cretan labyrinth.

clue.text: Privileged classes ignoring first item in list (5)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is left out

annotation.surface: A list drawn up that leaves the upper classes off the top.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First' looks as if it belongs with 'item in list' as in a first entry; it belongs to the deletion instruction instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: each line of a register, index or dictionary is called an entry.

clue.text: Pervasiveness from men working with cinema (9)

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged

annotation.surface: How widespread a film crew's influence is.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two parts of the fodder: nine letters from MEN plus CINEMA.
annotation.definitionFit: Immanence is the quality of being present throughout something, i.e. pervading it.

clue.text: Bulk of money earned for each journal submission? (5)

indicators.note: the bulk is most of it, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: PAY = money earned; its bulk is PA
per = for each, as in 'per head'

annotation.surface: An academic asking what a journal pays per article.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a paper is just one example of what might be submitted to a journal.
annotation.definitionFit: Academics submit papers to learned journals for publication.

clue.text: Verbose part cut in films (6)

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter
the shortened part goes inside the films

blocks.note: ROLE = part in a play or film, cut to ROL

annotation.surface: A wordy role trimmed down in the edit of a film.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Verbose part' a talky role; in fact 'Verbose' stands alone as the definition. P(ROL)IX.
annotation.definitionFit: Prolix means tediously long-winded, using too many words.

clue.text: Group of soldiers also covered by proposal (7)

indicators.note: the word is covered, i.e. enclosed, by the other

annotation.surface: A plan that also takes in a unit of troops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Covered by proposal' reads as 'included in the scheme'; here the covering is literal, one word physically wrapped round another.
annotation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small army unit, a subdivision of a company.

clue.text: Translation of Homer omitting nothing, but including unknown verse (5)

indicators.note: a translation puts the letters into a new order
the O is left out of the word
the Y is taken in among the letters

blocks.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

annotation.surface: A complete translation of Homer that somehow contains a line nobody knew.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Omitting nothing' reads as a faithful, full translation; here it literally means leave out the O.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyme can mean verse in general, as in 'nursery rhyme' or 'in rhyme'.

clue.text: Obsolete dispersal of seeds? Unable to consider anything new, perhaps (8)

definitions.text: Unable to consider anything new, perhaps

indicators.note: dispersed letters are scattered and rearranged

annotation.surface: A botanical note on an old way of scattering seed.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: someone obsessed can think only of one thing. 'Perhaps' admits this is one way of putting it.
annotation.definitionFit: An obsessed person's mind is fixed on one subject, leaving no room for anything new.

clue.text: God particle? A godsend, securing lead in sciences (5)

indicators.note: the boon holds the S fast inside it

annotation.surface: A physicist calling the discovery of the 'God particle' a godsend for science.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'God particle' is the popular nickname for the Higgs boson; the question mark marks the definition as an example of the class.
annotation.definitionFit: The Higgs boson, nicknamed the God particle, is one kind of boson.

clue.text: Music’s pulse — odd thing to drop it for a while (9)

definitions.note: adverbial phrase for an adjective: 'a job for a while' = 'a temporary job'

indicators.note: IT is dropped out of the word

blocks.note: tempo = the speed or beat of music
RARITY = an odd thing; drop IT

annotation.surface: A musician losing the beat for a moment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun for the pulse; it is the letters IT, removed from RARITY.
annotation.definitionFit: Something temporary lasts only for a while.

clue.text: Times function in cathedral city? Absolutely (7)

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the city

annotation.surface: Asking whether the Times newspaper operates in a cathedral city, and getting a firm yes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Times' at the start of a Times clue looks like the newspaper; it is the multiplication sign X. Ely is a small city in eastern England with a famous cathedral.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Exactly!' and 'Absolutely!' are both emphatic ways of agreeing.

clue.text: Back working with India — a little disagreeable? (7)

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

blocks.note: on = working, as a switched-on machine
India = I in the NATO alphabet
some = a little, as in 'some milk'

annotation.surface: Someone back at work alongside India, finding it a bit unpleasant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back working' reads as returning to a job; it is ON turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: Noisome means offensive or disagreeable, especially of a smell.

clue.text: Thames activity beginning to see a Parisian returning in Thames location (4-6)

indicators.note: only the first letter of 'see' is used
the French word comes back to front
the reversed word goes inside the place name

blocks.note: Wapping, a riverside district of East London

annotation.surface: A Frenchman going back to a riverside spot to watch something happen on the Thames.
annotation.walkthrough: Wapping is a district on the north bank of the Thames in East London. 'A Parisian' is a convention for a French article: UN, reversed to NU and set inside WAPPING.
annotation.definitionFit: Swan upping is the annual July census of mute swans on the Thames.

clue.text: Drunk old man with clarity impaired (9)

indicators.note: the word is damaged, so its letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An old man so drunk he cannot think clearly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paralytic' is British slang for extremely drunk. 'With' just joins PA to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang, paralytic means so drunk one can barely move.

clue.text: Boss never coming between king and bishop (4)

indicators.note: the word sits between the two letters

annotation.surface: A boss who never interferes between king and bishop, as on a chessboard or in a church quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boss' reads as a manager; here it is a round raised stud or knob, as on a shield.
annotation.definitionFit: A boss is a round protuberance, such as a knob on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Nature notes? Pen no good to capture sources of delightful sounds (8)

indicators.note: the pen and 'no good' take the letters inside
the source of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen

annotation.surface: A nature writer finding their pen not up to capturing lovely sounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pen' could be prison (BIRD), which even starts the answer, but here it is a biro, the British word for a ballpoint pen, split open to take the initials.
annotation.definitionFit: Birdsong is the natural world's music: nature's notes.

clue.text: Damage to lawn? Cut up about rook with company (8)

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word upside down, i.e. back to front
the reversed word goes around the R

blocks.note: to mow = to cut, turned up to WOM

annotation.surface: A gardener mowing a lawn damaged by a rook and friends.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rook' belongs on a lawn as a bird; here it is the chess piece R. 'Company' is a cast of actors, not guests.
annotation.definitionFit: A wormcast is the coil of soil a worm leaves on the surface, spoiling a neat lawn.

clue.text: Botched component of later course? (4)

blocks.note: British slang for useless or broken, like a dud
a boiled suet pudding, the 'later course' being dessert

annotation.surface: A faulty part of a later course of study.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' reads as a course of study; it is a course of a meal, the pudding. Duff is British slang for broken or useless, and plum duff is a steamed pudding.
annotation.definitionFit: Duff means dud or botched; plum duff is a pudding, served in the dessert course.

clue.text: Quality line receiving approval? On the contrary (7)

indicators.note: one word takes the other inside
swap the roles: approval receives line, not line approval

annotation.surface: Asking whether a quality product line is getting the go-ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: As written, the line would contain the approval; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so FAVOUR takes in L.
annotation.definitionFit: A flavour is a distinctive quality or character, as in 'a flavour of the East'.

clue.text: One looking to plunder drink coming round to enter message on page’s bottom (10)

indicators.note: the word turns round, back to front
the reversed word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a footer is text printed at the foot of a page

annotation.surface: A pirate after drink leaving a note at the bottom of a page.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One looking to plunder' sounds like a thirsty pirate after drink, which is exactly what the surface wants; only the first four words define.
annotation.definitionFit: A freebooter is a pirate or adventurer who lives by plunder.

clue.text: Court case finishing early with detectives turning up as small group (7)

definitions.note: adjective read as a phrase: 'triadic' = in the form of a group of three

indicators.note: the word stops one letter short
in a down clue, 'up' reverses the letters

blocks.note: TRIAL, with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A trial collapsing early when a small team of detectives shows up.
annotation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
annotation.definitionFit: Triadic means consisting of a triad, a group of three: a small group.

clue.text: Evidence of assault? Bachelor is covered in regret (6)

indicators.note: IS is wrapped by the regret

annotation.surface: A bachelor, covered in regret, showing evidence of an attack.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a bruise is one possible sign of an assault.
annotation.definitionFit: A bruise is a mark left by a blow, so it can be evidence of an assault.

clue.text: Dispute diminished one pursued by the French revolutionary (7)

indicators.note: the word is made smaller, losing its last letter
a revolution turns the word round

blocks.note: QUARRY = hunted prey, diminished to QUARR

annotation.surface: A row in which a weakened person is chased by a French revolutionary.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One pursued' is the quarry of a hunt. 'Diminished' sits before it but works on it; 'pursued by' then places EL after.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an angry disagreement between people is both a quarrel and a dispute.

clue.text: Seek peace, abandoning island around South (5)

definitions.note: verb: to quest is to seek

indicators.note: to abandon something is to leave it behind, so the island's I is left out of the word
what remains goes round the S

annotation.surface: Leaving an island to look for peace in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seek peace' reads as a single phrase; 'Seek' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary verb: knights quest for the Grail, meaning they go in search of it.

clue.text: The writer, with method, is penning start of racy autobiography of a sort (7)

indicators.note: IS pens, i.e. encloses, the letter
only the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the writer = the setter, so ME

annotation.surface: An author methodically writing the saucy opening of a life story.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is penning' looks like writing; in fact IS encloses R.
annotation.definitionFit: Memoirs are an account of one's own life, a kind of autobiography.

clue.text: Second Charlie overturned a hot drink (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters are turned over, bottom to top

blocks.note: Charlie = C in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Charlie, clumsily knocking over a second hot drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hot drink' looks like the definition; H is hot, and only 'drink' defines.
annotation.definitionFit: A mocha is a coffee drink flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: After end of course, understood one’s habitual response praising oneself (9)

definitions.note: participle phrase for an adjective: 'a praising-oneself man' = 'an egotistic man'

indicators.note: only the last letter is taken
the following pieces come after the E

blocks.note: got = understood, as in 'I got it'
a tic = a habitual twitch or reflex

annotation.surface: Once a course is over, someone's reflex is to boast about how well they did.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's' gives I plus the S of the possessive, a common crossword trick.
annotation.definitionFit: An egotistic person talks themselves up constantly.

clue.text: Poet to assess cutting 40 per cent, even cutting out middle section (5)

indicators.note: two of five letters, 40 per cent, are removed
the middle letters of the word are taken out

blocks.note: AUDIT = to assess; lose IT, two of its five letters

annotation.surface: A poet assessing cuts of 40 per cent, perhaps to a budget, and even cutting the middle section of a poem.
annotation.walkthrough: The percentage is exact: AUDIT has five letters, so 40 per cent is two letters, the IT at its end.
annotation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American poet of the 20th century.

clue.text: Fit cast on the radio (5)

indicators.note: a radio is heard, so the word is taken by sound

annotation.surface: A casting or fitness note for a radio play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fit cast' reads as a healthy cast of actors; 'Fit' is a spasm, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A throe is a violent spasm or pang, such as a fit.

clue.text: Confused style limiting advanced books (7)

indicators.note: the style sets limits on both sides of the letters, enclosing them

blocks.note: OT = Old Testament, a set of books

annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' is almost always OT or NT, the two Testaments of the Bible, in crosswords.
annotation.surface: A muddled way of writing that holds back advanced books.
annotation.definitionFit: Chaotic means in total confusion.
